AI Psychologist persona

A calm space to think out loud about stress, relationships and habits. The persona asks reflective questions and offers simple self-help techniques. It is an AI, not a licensed psychologist.

TL;DR
  • Best for reflecting on everyday stress, conflicts and habits you want to change.
  • It asks questions and suggests self-help techniques; it does not diagnose or treat.
  • If you are in crisis, call your local emergency number or a helpline right away.
Not therapy, not medical advice

This AI coach is a self-help tool. It is not a licensed psychologist, therapist or doctor, and it cannot diagnose or treat anything. If you are in danger or thinking about harming yourself, call your local emergency number now (112, 911 or 999 in many countries) or find a free, confidential helpline at findahelpline.com.

What this coach helps with

  • Putting a stressful situation into words
  • Preparing for a difficult conversation
  • Spotting patterns in your thoughts
  • Simple self-help techniques for everyday stress
  • Deciding whether to talk to a professional

Prompts you can copy

Copy a prompt, paste it into the Zehn AI Chat or any AI assistant, and replace the parts in [brackets] with your own details.

  1. I'd like to talk through something that's bothering me: [situation]. Ask me questions one at a time to help me understand how I feel.

  2. I keep thinking [thought]. Help me look at the evidence for and against it, like a thought record.

  3. I need to talk to [person] about [issue]. Help me plan what to say using “I” statements.

  4. I often feel [feeling] when [situation]. Help me notice what triggers it and one thing I could try next time.

  5. I procrastinate on [task] and then feel guilty. Help me understand what's behind it without judging me.

  6. Explain in simple words what burnout is and give me 5 questions to reflect on whether my workload is sustainable.

  7. Help me write a kind letter to myself about [mistake], the way I would write to a friend.

  8. I had an argument with [person]. Help me see the situation from their point of view, then from mine.

  9. Suggest three small daily habits that support mood, and help me choose one to start this week.

  10. I want to set a boundary with [person] about [issue]. Help me find the words and plan for their reaction.

  11. Ask me reflective questions about what matters most to me right now and summarise my answers.

  12. Help me prepare for my first appointment with a therapist: what to say, what to ask and what to expect.

Two example conversations

Written by the Intellect AI team to show the style of answers. Not a real user conversation.

ExamplePreparing a hard conversation

YouMy sister keeps cancelling our plans at the last minute and I'm hurt, but I don't want a fight.

PsychologistThat sounds frustrating, especially if the plans matter to you. One way to start: “When plans change last minute, I feel let down, because I look forward to seeing you. Could we find a way to plan that works for both of us?” How do you think she might react to that?

ExampleUntangling a worry

YouI made a mistake at work and I'm sure everyone thinks I'm useless now.

PsychologistLet's look at that thought together. What exactly happened, and what has anyone actually said? Sometimes our mind jumps from “I made a mistake” to “I am a failure”. What would you tell a colleague who made the same mistake?

Tips for better answers

  • Go at your own pace. You can ask it to slow down or change the subject at any time.
  • Use it to prepare for real conversations, then have them with real people.
  • Write down one insight at the end of each chat; it helps the next one.
  • If you notice the same heavy feelings for weeks, that is a good reason to see a professional.

Questions people ask

Is the AI Psychologist a real psychologist?

No. It is an AI persona that uses a reflective, supportive style of conversation. It is not licensed, cannot diagnose or treat any condition and does not know your history. It can help you put feelings into words and try simple self-help techniques. For ongoing problems, please see a qualified mental health professional.

What should I do in a mental health emergency?

If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call your local emergency number now, such as 112, 911 or 999. You can also contact a crisis helpline; findahelpline.com lists free, confidential services by country. Don't rely on an AI chat in an emergency. Reach a real person as fast as possible.

What is an AI psychologist persona good for?

It is good for everyday reflection: making sense of a stressful day, planning a difficult conversation, noticing unhelpful thought patterns and trying techniques like thought records or kind self-talk. Many people also use it to prepare questions before seeing a therapist. It works best as a supplement to real support.

Is it private to talk about feelings with an AI chat?

Treat any AI chat as a service run by a company, not a sealed diary. Avoid sharing full names, addresses, medical records or details that could identify other people. Describe situations in general terms. Read the privacy policy of the app you use, and keep the most sensitive matters for a professional.
